topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the complement lecture, framing its complexity and nomenclature.

topics.label: Fundamentals and Core Principles of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the core architecture of the complement cascade, its historical nomenclature, and the central biochemical role of C3.

topics.label: Complement Activation Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct recognition pathways that initiate complement and converge to reach the activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of Activated Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three primary downstream effector actions through which complement destroys pathogens and mediates inflammation.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and biochemical mechanisms that prevent complement from attacking host cells.

topics.label: Clinical Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the diverse clinical presentations and disease pathologies resulting from deficiencies in specific complement components and regulators.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how pathogens evolve strategies to resist complement clearance, highlighting mechanisms used by Staphylococcus aureus.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the discussion on complement and previews the next lecture on the adaptive immune system.
